description: API Gateways must enable access logging with proper retention

requirements.description: API Gateway stage has no access logging configuration at all
requirements.rationale: The rule requires access logging to be enabled. A stage with no access log settings violates this requirement. AWS docs identify access logging as the mechanism for capturing per-request data on API Gateway stages.

requirements.description: API Gateway stage has access logging configured with a destination pointing to a CloudWatch log group declared in the same template, and that log group has an explicit non-zero retention period
requirements.rationale: Access logging is enabled with a valid in-template destination, and the user resolved that any explicit non-zero retention is acceptable for 'proper retention'.

requirements.description: API Gateway stage has access logging configured pointing to a CloudWatch log group declared in the same template, but that log group has no retention configured (logs retained indefinitely)
requirements.rationale: The rule requires 'proper retention'. When retention is not specified on a CloudWatch log group, logs never expire, which fails the retention portion of the requirement. AWS docs (AWS::Logs::LogGroup RetentionInDays) state that omitting RetentionInDays causes log events not to expire.

requirements.description: API Gateway stage has access logging configured pointing to a CloudWatch log group declared in the same template, but that log group has retention explicitly set to zero or a non-positive value
requirements.rationale: A zero or non-positive retention is not a valid 'explicit non-zero retention' and effectively disables proper retention enforcement. The user resolution requires explicit non-zero retention.

requirements.description: API Gateway stage references an access log destination by ARN or name that is not declared anywhere in the template (external/pre-existing resource)
requirements.rationale: User-resolved decision: external resources are out of scope for IaC analysis. Access logging is enabled and the destination is managed elsewhere.

requirements.description: API Gateway stage has access logging configured with a destination that is a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream rather than a CloudWatch log group
requirements.rationale: User-resolved decision: Firehose is a valid access log destination. AWS docs confirm DestinationArn may reference a CloudWatch Logs log group or a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.

requirements.description: Access logging configuration block is present on the stage but contains no destination value (empty/missing destination)
requirements.rationale: Without a destination, no logs are actually delivered. AWS docs require both DestinationArn and Format to enable access logging.

requirements.description: API Gateway stage's access log destination value depends on a condition or input that cannot be resolved at analysis time
requirements.rationale: The rule cannot assert non-compliance when critical configuration values are unknown at analysis time; flagging would produce false positives.

requirements.description: API Gateway V2 (HTTP or WebSocket) stage has no access log settings configured
requirements.rationale: User-resolved decision: the rule applies to both REST and V2 stages. V2 stages without access log settings violate the same requirement.

requirements.description: API Gateway V2 stage has access logging enabled pointing to an in-template CloudWatch log group with explicit non-zero retention
requirements.rationale: V2 stages are in scope per user resolution; this configuration satisfies both the logging and retention requirements.

requirements.description: API Gateway stage has access logging enabled, but the referenced in-template log group's retention value cannot be resolved at analysis time. This includes retention set from a template parameter with no default, which preprocessing substitutes with the placeholder string 'DEFAULT'.
requirements.rationale: The rule cannot definitively assert that retention is missing or invalid when the value is unresolvable; flagging would risk false positives. The 'DEFAULT' placeholder means the value is chosen at deploy time, not that the author wrote an invalid retention, so it belongs here rather than under REQ-12. A parameter default that does resolve to a numeric string is a real value and is judged on that value.

requirements.description: API Gateway stage has access logging enabled and points to an in-template log group, but the log group's retention is set to a value the rule does not recognize as a valid CloudWatch retention period (e.g., a non-numeric or otherwise invalid value)
requirements.rationale: An invalid retention value will not produce the intended retention behavior. Per the user resolution, an explicit non-zero, valid retention is required.
